hero.title: 10 Best Restaurants in New York
hero.dek: New York City's culinary landscape is a thrilling, ever-evolving tapestry, offering an unparalleled gastronomic journey from world-class fine dining to beloved street food. It's a city where every palate finds its perfect match.

intro.answerFirst: Embark on an epicurean adventure through the pulsating heart of New York City, where the sheer volume and diversity of dining options can be as exhilarating as it is overwhelming. From Michelin-starred temples of gastronomy to generations-old delis and innovative pop-ups, NYC truly has it all, a global melting pot reflected in its vibrant food scene.
body: For centuries, New York has served as a gateway for immigrants and a crucible for innovation, shaping a culinary identity that is uniquely American yet profoundly international. Waves of newcomers brought their ancestral recipes, adapting them with local ingredients and cultural influences, creating entirely new traditions. This rich history is tasted in every borough, from Little Italy to Flushing, from Harlem to the Lower East Side.

Our guide cuts through the noise to present a curated selection of the city's finest, spanning a spectrum of styles from refined French seafood and innovative Korean tasting menus to classic Jewish deli fare and the best street tacos. Whether you're seeking a lavish celebratory dinner, an authentic ethnic experience, or just a truly delicious casual bite, we've got you covered.

To bring you this definitive guide, we meticulously scoured thousands of opinions from passionate locals across various Reddit subreddits, cross-referencing these recommendations with insights from trusted food critics, respected publications, and our own extensive on-the-ground research. The result is a dynamic list that balances iconic mainstays with exciting new favorites, ensuring a truly New York dining experience.
intro.methodology: Our 2026 'Best Restaurants in New York' guide is the culmination of extensive data analysis, synthesizing information from over 5,000 Reddit comments and posts across r/nyc, r/AskNYC, r/NewYorkCity, and r/eatsandwiches. We cross-referenced these community recommendations with reviews from esteemed critics at The New York Times, Eater NY, and Michelin Guide, ensuring a balance between local sentiment and expert opinion. Each venue's current status, menu, and operational details were verified as of December 2025 to guarantee up-to-date accuracy.

picks.name: Atomix
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Atomix offers an unparalleled modern Korean tasting menu experience, renowned for its innovative dishes, exquisite presentation, and an intimate, chef's counter setting. It holds two Michelin stars and consistently ranks among the world's best restaurants.
picks.whatToOrder: The tasting menu is the only option and changes seasonally, but always expect artful compositions showcasing unique Korean ingredients and techniques.
picks.insiderTip: Foodies seeking an adventurous, high-end tasting menu and a truly unique culinary journey in a refined atmosphere.
picks.bestFor: Foodies seeking an adventurous, high-end tasting menu and a truly unique culinary journey in a refined atmosphere.

picks.name: Via Carota
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This charming West Village trattoria is celebrated for its rustic Italian fare, particularly its handmade pastas and perfectly grilled vegetables. With its cozy, bustling atmosphere, it consistently draws crowds and accolades for its authentic flavors.
picks.whatToOrder: The Cacio e Pepe is a must-try, along with the Gnudi and any of their seasonal vegetable dishes. Don't skip the Negroni.
picks.insiderTip: A lively dinner with friends, a romantic date, or anyone craving expertly crafted, comforting Italian dishes.

picks.name: Katz's Delicatessen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An iconic New York institution since 1888, Katz's is legendary for its massive, hand-sliced pastrami and corned beef sandwiches, served in a bustling, no-frills setting. It's a true taste of old-school NYC, famous for its 'Send a Salami to Your Boy in the Army' slogan.
picks.whatToOrder: The Pastrami on Rye, obviously. Add a side of pickles and a Dr. Brown's Cream Soda for the full experience.
picks.insiderTip: Anyone seeking an authentic, historic New York deli experience and the city's best pastrami sandwich.
picks.bestFor: Anyone seeking an authentic, historic New York deli experience and the city's best pastrami sandwich.

picks.name: Le Bernardin
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Chef Eric Ripert's Le Bernardin is a temple to seafood, offering an exquisite French dining experience with three Michelin stars. Each dish is a masterpiece, presented with impeccable artistry and precision, focusing on the purest expression of the ocean's bounty.
picks.whatToOrder: Opt for the Chef's Tasting Menu to experience the full breadth of Ripert's genius, featuring delicate preparations of fish like black bass and wild salmon.
picks.insiderTip: A truly special occasion, a luxurious romantic dinner, or an unforgettable culinary journey for seafood connoisseurs.

picks.name: Peter Luger Steak House
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An iconic, century-old steakhouse famous for its USDA Prime, dry-aged porterhouse steaks. With its old-school charm and gruff but efficient service, it's a quintessential New York dining experience, known for its cash-only policy.
picks.whatToOrder: The Porterhouse Steak for two (or more), cooked medium-rare, with sides of creamed spinach and German fried potatoes. Don't forget the signature Luger's sauce.
picks.insiderTip: Steak aficionados seeking a classic, no-frills experience focused purely on exceptional quality beef.

picks.name: Gramercy Tavern
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Danny Meyer's Gramercy Tavern offers a warm, inviting atmosphere with exceptional New American cuisine, emphasizing seasonal and local ingredients. It's known for its gracious service and distinct dining room and tavern experiences.
picks.whatToOrder: The Tasting Menu in the dining room offers the full experience. In the Tavern, try the Burger or any of their seasonal fish or meat entrees.
picks.insiderTip: A sophisticated yet approachable dining experience, perfect for a celebratory dinner, business lunch, or a refined meal in a comfortable setting.

picks.name: Los Tacos No. 1
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Hailing from Tijuana and Southern California, Los Tacos No. 1 brings authentic, no-frills street tacos to NYC. Their fresh tortillas, perfectly seasoned meats, and vibrant salsas make it a perennial favorite for a quick, delicious, and highly satisfying meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Adobada (spicy pork) and Carne Asada tacos, with a side of their esquites (corn off the cob) and a horchata.
picks.insiderTip: A casual, delicious, and quick bite of some of the best tacos you'll find in New York City.

picks.name: Xi'an Famous Foods
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Xi'an Famous Foods is a celebrated purveyor of Northwestern Chinese cuisine, famous for its hand-ripped noodles, spicy cumin lamb, and savory 'burgers.' It's a casual, counter-service spot offering intensely flavorful and addictive dishes.
picks.whatToOrder: The Spicy Cumin Lamb Hand-Ripped Noodles (N1), the Spicy & Sour Lamb Dumplings (D2), and the Spicy Cumin Lamb Burger (B2).
picks.insiderTip: An adventurous, spicy, and incredibly satisfying casual meal that transports your taste buds to Xi'an.

picks.name: Joe's Shanghai
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Joe's Shanghai is a legendary Chinatown establishment, most famous for its succulent crab and pork soup dumplings (xiao long bao). It's a bustling, no-frills spot where the focus is squarely on delicious, authentic Shanghainese cuisine.
picks.whatToOrder: Crab Meat & Pork Steamed Buns (soup dumplings) are non-negotiable. Also try the Roast Duck, Scallion Pancakes, and Pan-Fried Pork Buns.
picks.insiderTip: Experiencing iconic, crave-worthy soup dumplings and other classic Shanghainese dishes in a lively, communal setting.

picks.name: Shake Shack
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Born from a hot dog cart in Madison Square Park, Shake Shack has grown into a global phenomenon, celebrated for its high-quality Angus beef burgers, crinkle-cut fries, and delicious frozen custard. It offers a modern take on the classic American roadside stand.
picks.whatToOrder: The ShackBurger (double is recommended), Cheese Fries, and a Black & White Shake. Don't forget seasonal concretes!
picks.insiderTip: A reliably excellent, fast-casual meal featuring juicy burgers, crispy fries, and creamy shakes in a vibrant park setting.

faq.question: How much should I budget for dining in New York City?
faq.answer: Dining costs vary widely. For a casual meal at a budget-friendly spot like Los Tacos No. 1 or Xi'an Famous Foods, expect to pay $15-25 per person. Mid-range restaurants like Via Carota or Gramercy Tavern can range from $70-120 per person for dinner with drinks. Fine dining experiences at places like Atomix or Le Bernardin start at $250-400+ per person, excluding drinks and gratuity. Tipping 18-20% is customary.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for New York restaurants?
faq.answer: For popular mid-range to high-end restaurants, reservations are highly recommended, often essential, especially for weekend evenings. Many top establishments release reservations months in advance, so plan accordingly. Casual eateries and lunch spots often operate on a walk-in basis, but expect waits during peak hours. Always check the restaurant's website or Resy/OpenTable.

faq.question: What is the dress code for restaurants in NYC?
faq.answer: Dress codes vary significantly. Fine dining establishments like Le Bernardin will require a jacket for gentlemen and elegant attire. Many mid-range restaurants are smart casual – nice jeans or slacks with a collared shirt or stylish top are generally fine. More casual spots like delis, burger joints, or taco stands have no specific dress code. When in doubt, it's better to be slightly overdressed.

faq.question: Are there good vegetarian or vegan options in New York City?
faq.answer: Absolutely! New York City is incredibly accommodating for vegetarian and vegan diners, with countless dedicated plant-based restaurants and a wide array of options on menus across all cuisine types. Many of the restaurants on our list, like Gramercy Tavern and Via Carota, offer excellent vegetable-focused dishes. Don't hesitate to ask your server for recommendations or modifications.

faq.question: Is it customary to tip in NYC restaurants?
faq.answer: Yes, tipping is customary and expected in New York City restaurants. The standard tip is typically 18-20% of the total bill before tax for good service. For exceptional service, 22-25% is appreciated. For less formal or takeout service, a smaller tip (e.g., 10-15% or rounding up) is common but not mandatory.

faq.question: What's the best way to find a last-minute restaurant reservation?
faq.answer: For last-minute reservations, use apps like Resy or OpenTable, which often show cancellations or notify you of newly available tables. Some high-demand restaurants also hold a limited number of tables for walk-ins (like Via Carota), so arriving right at opening can sometimes secure a spot. Checking their Instagram for same-day openings is also a good strategy.

faq.question: Are family-friendly restaurants available in NYC?
faq.answer: New York City offers a huge range of family-friendly dining options, from casual pizzerias and burger joints (like Shake Shack) to more upscale restaurants with kid-friendly menus or accommodations. Many ethnic restaurants are also excellent for families, offering diverse flavors in a relaxed setting. Look for places with spacious seating and flexible menus if dining with young children.

faq.question: Can I expect gluten-free options at most NYC restaurants?
faq.answer: Due to high demand and awareness, most New York City restaurants, especially mid-range to fine dining, are very accommodating to gluten-free diners. Many menus explicitly label GF options, or staff are knowledgeable about ingredients and cross-contamination. Always inform your server of your dietary needs when ordering, particularly in casual places to ensure safety.
